chunks: Ali narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Durust, from Abu al-Mu'za, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah included the parents with all the heirs of fixed shares, so He did not reduce them from the sixth for each one of them; and He included the husband and the wife with all the heirs of inheritance, so He did not reduce them from the quarter and the eighth.
ai.seo_question: How are parents and spouses treated in Islamic inheritance when other heirs are present?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential principle of 'adding' (idkhal) parents and spouses to the inheritance pool, ensuring their fixed shares (one-sixth each for parents, one-quarter for husband, one-eighth for wife) remain intact regardless of other heirs. In Shia fiqh, this distinguishes their status from other relatives whose shares might be reduced by the presence of closer kin, highlighting the specific protection granted to these primary relatives in the distribution of estate. This ruling is foundational in resolving conflicts between fixed-share heirs and residuary heirs (asabah).
